statements.status_notes: The built image SBOM locates jackson-core 2.21.2 and 3.1.2 inside hazelcast-5.7.0.jar in nifi-hazelcast-services-nar, and jackson-core 2.21.3 inside parquet-jackson-1.17.1.jar in nifi-iceberg-parquet-writer-nar. NiFi's Maven dependency management cannot directly replace these embedded copies. Remediation requires upgrading the enclosing artifacts: Parquet 1.18.0 embeds jackson-core 2.22.1 but requires compatibility validation, while Hazelcast currently has no newer release that embeds fixed jackson-core 2.x and 3.x versions.

The jackson-core instances used by neo4j have been bumped to a fixed version. The remaining jackson-core is shaded and relocated inside parquet-jackson JARs, which no fixed parquet release replaces. The vulnerable code is the non-blocking async parser, which accumulates integer digits across chunked feeds without enforcing the number-length constraint. The parquet libraries never create a non-blocking parser, so the vulnerable path is not reachable.

jackson-core 2.18.6 is bundled inside ray_dist.jar, which ships with the Ray Python package. The vulnerable path is the non-blocking async parser, which accumulates integer digits across chunked feeds without enforcing the number-length constraint, and is reachable only through Ray's Java runtime. This image ships no Java runtime, so Ray never starts a Java worker and the bundled classes are never loaded.

Jackson Core async parser fails to enforce maxNumberLength constraint in chunked-feed scenarios, allowing memory exhaustion. Fixed in 2.18.8 and 2.21.4. The vulnerable dependency is embedded in compiled application JARs and cannot be patched via JAR replacement. Waiting for upstream SonarQube to upgrade jackson-core.

jackson-core 2.21.3 is shaded inside parquet-hadoop-bundle 1.17.1 (latest on Maven Central). DHI forces that bundle over upstream 1.17.0, but no published parquet-hadoop-bundle yet embeds the 2.21.4 fix for GHSA-r7wm-3cxj-wff9. The vulnerability affects async JSON parsing with unbounded number length, but Elasticsearch's typical deployment behind reverse proxies with request size limits provides some mitigation.

GHSA-r7wm-3cxj-wff9 affects only the shaded jackson-core 2.19.2 copy inside hazelcast-5.6.0.jar, not the classpath copy (forced to 2.21.4 via resolutionStrategy). The shaded parser has no call sites in DataHub code; all JSON parsing flows through the fixed classpath copy. Hazelcast 5.7.0 will bundle the fix.

GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq is a missing maxNumberLength validation in jackson-core's non-blocking (async) parser (NonBlockingUtf8JsonParserBase skips the resetInt()/resetFloat() length checks), fixed in jackson-core 2.21.1. The 2.19.2 copy Scout flags in this image is not the classpath jackson-core: upstream DataHub v1.5.0.7 pins jacksonVersion 2.21.3, and the fat jar's BOOT-INF/lib carries jackson-core-2.21.3.jar, which already contains the fix. The 2.19.2 copy exists only as classes relocated to com.hazelcast.shaded.com.fasterxml.jackson.core inside hazelcast-5.6.0.jar (identified via its bundled pom.properties), where Gradle's resolutionStrategy cannot reach it. Verified against the built mce-consumer-job.jar: a byte-level scan of every class in the fat jar and all 576 bundled libraries found zero classes referencing com/hazelcast/shaded/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/json/async, and no Hazelcast class invokes createNonBlockingByteArrayParser or createNonBlockingParser on the relocated copy, so the vulnerable async parser in the 2.19.2 copy has no call sites. The async call sites that do exist (rest.li entitystream decoders, vertx JsonParserImpl, spring-web Jackson2Tokenizer) bind to the fixed 2.21.3 classpath copy, and AWS SDK's third-party-jackson-core 2.32.25 is a separately versioned artifact. The shaded fix lands with Hazelcast 5.7.0 (bundles jackson-core 2.21.2); a 5.6 to 5.7 Hazelcast bump is upstream-managed and out of scope for a CVE remediation. This basis must be revisited if a future DataHub release starts feeding data through Hazelcast's relocated async parser.
